blocks: What medicines actually do inside your body.
It acts in three places at once: the brain, the stomach and the pancreas.
In the pancreas it unlocks insulin and holds back glucagon, so blood sugar comes down.
It copies two gut hormones, GLP-1 and GIP, and docks on their receptors.
Chemists joined the two copies into one molecule and added a fatty tail so it lasts days in the blood.
It also slows the stomach exit, so food leaves later and you stay full.
In the main trial the highest dose lost far more weight than placebo.
On average people lost twenty point nine percent of their weight.
One researcher called it the biggest change in obesity care in decades.
Insulin came in 1922, the first GLP-1 drug in 2005, semaglutide in 2017 and tirzepatide in 2022.
It is a prescription drug and nausea is common at first.
